l-001.evidence: Query seq 12 (FATAL grouped by user.name, 20:30–20:37) returns 6 rows in `observed` — root (152), and dbadmin/pgadmin/reporting/superuser/backup at 10 each, all first_seen 20:31:32.05–20:31:32.21 and last_seen 20:32:03.26–20:32:03.42 — whereas all three live controls (C-21d/C-28d/C-35d) return exactly one row, user.name root (5760/7200/7200). The distinguishing field is user.name, which these queries surface directly. Query seq 6 corroborates through `message`: the day-scoped prefix histogram carries 28 rows including `password authentication failed for user "backup"/"dbadmin"/"pgadmin"/"reporting"/"superuser"/"admin"/"postgres"` and `User "postgres" has no password assigned`, while every control returns only the two root-prefix rows. Siblings disagree: seq 10 and seq 0 show only root/FATAL/DETAIL content identical to baseline, and the Zeek queries (seq 13/14/23/25) differ from their zero-row controls solely in source.ip/destination.ip/zeek.session_id/event.id, which environment_notes marks unstable and therefore non-evidential.

l-002.evidence: All five queries in this lead are `cmdb.*` templates (host-trust-edges ×3, list-all-hosts, list-office-ws-hosts), which `environment_notes.state_and_lookup_systems` designates as configuration/entity lookups carrying no `@timestamp` bounds — hence the empty `baseline` array is expected, not a missing measurement. The payloads return entity records: db-1 with `service: {kind: postgres, port: 5432}` and `trust_edges_out: []`, office-ws-1 and office-ws-2 with `trust_edges_out: []`, and a `total: 11` host roster in which only web-1, web-2, jump-box-1, config-mgmt-1 and scanner-1 list `db-1` as a trust edge. Seq 0 is `unreadable`, but it is a duplicate host-trust-edges lookup on the same state system, so it cannot change the classification. No event-stream field is surfaced anywhere in this lead, so there is nothing to baseline-diff.

l-003.evidence: The two identity queries (seq 0, 1) return an entity record — enabled true, realm_role developer, authorized_hosts dev-ws-1/jump-box-1/office-ws-1, and authorized false / via null for db-1 — which is current configuration with no timestamp bounds and therefore no baseline-diff semantics. The two ES|QL queries decide the lead: seq 2 returns one row of events=0, logins=0, login_error=0, logouts=0, first_seen=null, last_seen=null, and all three live controls (C-21d, C-28d, C-35d) return exactly the same all-zero row. Seq 3's stream-health count returns events=0 in the observed window and events=0 in all three live controls, so the keycloak event stream is empty in both observed and baseline — an empty observed window against an empty live baseline is not suppression. No surfaced field (events, logins, login_error, logouts, first_seen, last_seen) differs from baseline in any direction.

l-005.evidence: The `baseline` block is an empty list — no control payload exists for any of the six queries, so there is nothing to compare the observed window against. The observed window is far from empty: seq 2/4/5 each return 12 rows, dominated by two 600-count rows ("password authentication failed for user \"root\"" and the matching "Role \"root\" does not exist." pg_hba line 99 message, user.name root, spanning 20:20:04.670Z–20:44:54.679Z), plus ten 10-count rows for dbadmin, backup, pgadmin, superuser and reporting confined to 20:31:32–20:32:03. Seq 1 returned row_count 0 while its near-identical sibling seq 2 returned 12, and seq 0 and seq 3 are unreadable, but neither fact decides the lead. What would settle it is a control run of the seq 4 or seq 5 ES|QL over a live shifted window showing whether these user.name/message pairs and their counts are routine on db-1.
